title: Spreadsheets with Excel
subtitle: Enter, format and analyse data; write formulas and functions; build charts and tables.
outcomes: Enter, edit and format data professionally
Write formulas with relative and absolute references
Use statistical, logical, lookup and finance functions
Present data with charts, tables and conditional formatting

pool.q: In a range reference such as A1:D10, what do the two cells mean?
options: The top-left and bottom-right corners of the range
The first and last rows only
Two separate cells, nothing in between
pool.explain: The range includes every cell in the rectangle between them.
pool.evidence: The first cell is the top left corner of the range, and the second cell is the lower right corner of the range.

pool.q: Taking a simple view, what is Excel?
options: A word processor for long documents
A tool for entering quantitative data into a spreadsheet and applying calculations
pool.explain: Those calculations then support decisions.
pool.evidence: Excel is a tool that allows you to enter quantitative data into an electronic spreadsheet to apply one or many mathematical computations

pool.q: What does the book advise when you type numbers into a worksheet?
options: Always type a dollar sign before money values
Avoid adding formatting symbols such as dollar signs and commas
Type numbers as text so they line up
Put each digit in its own cell
pool.explain: Type the raw number and apply number formats afterwards, so Excel can calculate with it.
pool.evidence: it is best to avoid adding any formatting symbols such as dollar signs and commas.

pool.q: Why might a cell show symbols instead of the number you typed?
options: The column is too narrow to fit the entry
pool.explain: Widen the column to see the value.
pool.evidence: This is because the column is too narrow to fit the entry you typed.

pool.q: Which key lets you edit the contents of the active cell?
pool.explain: F2 puts the cursor inside the cell's existing content.
pool.evidence: Activate the cell that is to be edited and press the F2 key on your keyboard.

pool.q: What does the book insist on after entering numbers into a worksheet?
pool.explain: A single mistyped number can change every result that depends on it.
pool.evidence: It is very important to proofread your worksheet carefully, especially when you have entered numbers.

pool.q: Why is improving a worksheet's visual appearance important?
options: It makes the formulas calculate faster
It is required to save the file
It makes the worksheet a more valuable tool for making decisions
pool.explain: Clear formatting helps you and colleagues read the data correctly.
pool.evidence: Enhancing the visual appearance of a worksheet is a critical step in creating a valuable tool for you or your coworkers when making key decisions.

pool.q: What is the benefit of the Wrap Text command?
options: It reduces the need to widen columns for multi-word headings
pool.explain: The heading wraps onto several lines within the cell.
pool.evidence: The benefit of using the Wrap Text command is that it significantly reduces the need to expand the column width to accommodate multiword column headings.

pool.q: In Excel, what is adding custom lines to a worksheet called?
pool.explain: A top border above a total row is a common example.
pool.evidence: In Excel, adding custom lines to a worksheet is known as adding borders.

pool.q: What happens when numbers in the cells a formula references are changed?
options: You must type the formula again
pool.explain: That is why formulas should reference cells rather than typed numbers.
pool.evidence: when the numbers in the cells that are referenced are changed, Excel automatically recalculates the formula and produces a new result

pool.q: When should a formula use a constant number instead of a cell reference?
options: When the value will not change, like 12 months in a year
pool.explain: Values that may change belong in cells.
pool.evidence: In this formula, a number, or constant, is used instead of a cell reference because it will not change.

pool.q: When are functions more efficient than formulas?
options: When you apply a mathematical process to a group of cells
When you only add two numbers
When the workbook has one sheet
pool.explain: =SUM(B2:B50) is quicker and safer than adding fifty cell references by hand.
pool.evidence: Functions are more efficient than formulas when you are applying a mathematical process to a group of cells.

pool.q: How are a function's arguments written?
options: Separated by spaces after an equals sign
Always enclosed in parentheses after the function name
In a separate dialog box only
pool.explain: For example =AVERAGE(C3:C14).
pool.evidence: After the function name comes the arguments for the function, which are always enclosed in parentheses.

pool.q: What is the principal of a loan?
options: The item used to secure the loan
The amount of money borrowed from the lender
pool.explain: The PMT function uses the rate, number of periods and principal to calculate payments.
pool.evidence: The amount of money that is borrowed from the lender is called the principal of the loan.

pool.q: Which function calculates monthly loan payments?
pool.explain: It works for car loans and mortgages alike.
pool.evidence: Use the PMT function to calculate monthly car loan payments.

pool.q: What is a loan?
options: An agreement to borrow money from a lender and repay it over a set period
pool.explain: The amount borrowed is the principal.
pool.evidence: A loan is a contractual agreement in which money is borrowed from a lender and paid back over a specific period of time.

pool.q: How should you reference cells when applying a statistical function to a contiguous range?
options: List every cell separated by plus signs
Use a cell range: two cell locations separated by a colon
Type the values directly into the function
pool.explain: A range like B2:B20 covers every cell between the two corners.
pool.evidence: Make sure you use a cell range (two cell locations separated by a colon) when applying a statistical function to a contiguous range of cells.

pool.q: In a VLOOKUP function, what is the Table_array?
options: The range (table) where the lookup values and the values to return are located
The value you want to find
pool.explain: The four arguments are Lookup_value, Table_array, Col_index_num and Range_lookup.
pool.evidence: The Table_array is the range (table) where the lookup values and the values you want returned by the function are located.

pool.q: What is the best thing about Conditional Formatting, according to the book?
options: It permanently changes the cell values
It is flexible, applying formatting only when certain conditions are met
pool.explain: Data bars, colour scales and cell rules highlight the values that matter.
pool.evidence: The best thing about Conditional Formatting is that it is flexible, applying specified formatting only when certain conditions are met.

pool.q: What is the primary purpose of a chart?
options: To present quantitative information to an audience
pool.explain: Choose the chart type from the message you want to communicate.
pool.evidence: the primary purpose of a chart is to present quantitative information to an audience.

pool.q: Before choosing which data to chart, what must you identify?
options: The message or idea you want to communicate
The largest number in the sheet
pool.explain: Not all data in a worksheet belongs on a chart.
pool.evidence: To determine what data should be used when creating a chart, you must first identify the message or idea that you want to communicate to an audience.

pool.q: Which chart type shows each part's percent of the total?
pool.explain: Line charts show trends over time; column charts compare values.
pool.evidence: Learn how to use a pie chart to show the percent of the total for a data set.

pool.q: When is a line chart preferred over a column chart?
options: When showing the percent of a total
When presenting data over long periods of time
pool.explain: Column charts become cluttered beyond about twenty bars; lines show long trends clearly.
pool.evidence: a line chart is preferred over a column chart when presenting data over long periods of time.

pool.q: Why are formatting commands applied to a chart?
options: To make the chart easier to read
pool.explain: The same reason they are applied to a worksheet.
pool.evidence: Formatting commands are applied to a chart for the same reason they are applied to a worksheet: they make the chart easier to read.

pool.q: What is a data series?
options: An item being displayed graphically on a chart
pool.explain: Each series can be formatted separately, for example its colour.
pool.evidence: A data series is an item that is being displayed graphically on a chart.

pool.q: What does Excel do automatically when you add new data to a table?
options: It expands the table and applies its formatting, such as banded rows
It turns the data into a chart
pool.explain: Tables keep their structure as they grow.
pool.evidence: Excel will also automatically expand the table to accommodate new data entries and allows for automatic formatting, such as recoloring of banded rows or columns.

pool.q: Why is planning a table's layout vital?
pool.explain: A consistent structure keeps records accurate and usable.
pool.evidence: Structuring and planning table layouts is vital for data integrity.

pool.q: Why refer to a table by its name rather than by its range?
options: Ranges cannot be used in formulas
It is easier to refer to later, especially in workbooks with many tables
pool.explain: Table names can also appear automatically as you build formulas.
pool.evidence: Referring to the table by name rather than by range will make it easier to refer to a table in the future

pool.q: What does a table's Total Row let you do?
options: Choose a summary function, such as Sum, Average or Count, for each column
pool.explain: It is a quick tool for data analysis.
pool.evidence: From the total row drop-down, you can select a function, like Average, Count, Count Numbers, Max, Min, Sum, StdDev, Var, and more.

pool.q: What are the fields you choose to sort by called?
pool.explain: You can sort by several keys in levels.
pool.evidence: The field or fields you select to sort are called sort keys.

pool.q: What happens to rows hidden by a filter?
options: They move to a new sheet
They are sorted to the bottom
They are hidden, not deleted, and reappear when the filter is removed
pool.explain: Filtering changes only what you see.
pool.evidence: The information that does not display is not deleted, it is just hidden

pool.q: What is a PivotTable?
options: A table that rotates its text
A list of all sheets in a workbook
A powerful tool that calculates, summarises and analyses table data to compare patterns and trends
A chart type for showing proportions
pool.explain: PivotTables use four areas — Rows, Columns, Values and Filters.
pool.evidence: A PivotTable is a powerful tool that calculates, summarizes, and analyzes table data to compare, patterns, and trends.

pool.q: What can you do with the sheets in an Excel file?
options: Move, copy, delete and rename them
pool.explain: Organising sheets keeps multi-sheet workbooks consistent.
pool.evidence: You can easily move, copy, delete, and rename sheets in your Excel file.

pool.q: What is the benefit of grouping several sheets?
options: It protects the sheets from editing
You can enter formulas once and have them appear in all the grouped sheets
It merges them into one sheet
pool.explain: Remember to ungroup afterwards — every change applies to all grouped sheets.
pool.evidence: By grouping all the month sheets together, we can enter each of the formulas once and have them appear in all the sheets.

pool.q: Besides the right-click menu, how can you rename a sheet?
options: Drag the tab to the right
Save the file with a new name
pool.explain: Clear sheet names make workbooks easier to navigate.
pool.evidence: you can also double-click a sheet tab name to rename it

pool.q: What do 3-D references in formulas allow you to do?
options: Use data from one or more sheets on another sheet
Reference cells in other workbooks only
Lock cells so they cannot be edited
pool.explain: A Summary sheet often totals the same cell across many monthly sheets.
pool.evidence: 3-D references in formulas allow you to use data from one or more sheets on another sheet.

pool.q: What is the Summary sheet in a multi-sheet workbook for?
options: Presenting totals from the other sheets in one place
pool.explain: It gives a quick synopsis of all the other sheets.
pool.evidence: The Summary sheet in many multiple sheet workbooks is utilized to present totaled information from the other sheets in the file.

pool.q: Where is the Summary sheet usually placed?
options: As the first sheet in the file
pool.explain: Readers see the overview before the detail.
pool.evidence: the Summary sheet is usually the first sheet in multiple sheet files

pool.q: What is an Excel template?
options: A backup copy of a workbook
A predefined pattern for a spreadsheet that has already been created for you
pool.explain: Templates save the time of designing common files such as budgets or calendars from scratch.
pool.evidence: A template is a predefined pattern for a spreadsheet that has already been created for you.
